slot_note: Seed ET08 (analytical_tasks/07_data_extraction_conformation, header and Situation only): an aid consortium's IATI publications and the decision where to open three country coordination offices; the world, the decision and the quantity kept, the pitfall re-found from the data.
niche: aid statistics compiled from a donor collaborative's IATI publications: the members' money followed through two pooled funds with different contribution cycles to the countries where it is spent
stakeholder_role: head of data and learning at a donor collaborative's secretariat

spine.entity: one IATI transaction (a commitment, a payment out, a receipt or an expenditure) on one activity, as its publisher reported it
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the IATI Datastore's flattened transaction layout)

world.geography: International: a London-based donor collaborative funding maternal and newborn health programmes in East Africa, the Sahel and South Asia
world.org_type: donor collaborative of foundations and agencies, and the pooled funds and organisations they fund

driver: Spending done through commingled intermediaries is credited to the original sources by their share of the money each intermediary held when it paid out, which for an intermediary that collects in one period and pays out in the next is the previous period's inflow mix, not the current one, and for one that pays out each inflow at once is the current one, carried into an intermediary funded by another; the current-period inflow share, the lifetime share and the receipts-before-payment share each rank a different wrong set.
driver_concrete: Each implementer's 2025 spending is credited to the members by the member share of the money its funder held when it paid: the global fund collects in the last quarter and pays the collection out the next year, so its 2025 grants carried the members' 31.7 per cent of its 2024 collection, not the 75 per cent of the 2025 collection received after its last 2025 grant; the Sahel fund pays each January round out the same year, so its 2025 grants carried the 2025 round's mix with the global fund's part at 31.7 per cent; the year's contribution share (Rwanda, Uganda, Mali), the lifetime share (Rwanda, Kenya, Uganda) and the share of contributions received before each payment (Rwanda, Kenya, Tanzania) each miss Rwanda, Kenya and Mali.
stump: The default path opens the offices in Rwanda, Uganda and Mali because it credits each pooled fund's 2025 spending by the members' share of the contributions paid into it in 2025, while the global fund paid its 2025 grants out of the 2024 collection it held, when the members' share was 31.7 per cent, not the 75 per cent of the 2025 collection that arrived after its last 2025 grant; credited by the money each fund held when it paid, Kenya replaces Uganda.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who converts every currency at its value date, keeps the implementers' 2025 expenditure, identifies each activity's funder and credits each pooled fund's spending by the members' share of its 2025 contributions (the year's imputed share), the global fund's money in the Sahel fund carrying the global fund's share, opens the offices in Rwanda, Uganda and Mali; with the share of every contribution the funds have received, Rwanda, Kenya and Uganda.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is aid statistics' imputed flow, each intermediary's country spending credited to its funders by their share of the resources that paid for it, carried through every layer of the delivery chain; the compilers' same-year contribution share stands in for that only while a fund's donor mix is steady, and an expert matches a fund that collects in arrears to the year of money it spent. With a retailer's nouns there are no pooled funds of commingled donor money, no contribution cycle and no delivery chain, so the task stops reading.
notes: Drawn 2026-10-13 for wave 2 under the 10/10 rules.
